questions.prompt: In this course, what is the displayed two-qubit bitstring order?

options.text: Always alphabetical order of the gate names
Measurement time order regardless of register labels

questions.explanation: q0 is the least significant bit and is written on the right. Wire position and printed significance must be kept separate.

questions.prompt: How many complex amplitudes describe a general pure three-qubit state?
questions.explanation: There are 2 cubed computational-basis strings. Each basis string has one amplitude.

questions.prompt: In CX(q0,q1), which qubit is flipped when the control is 1?
questions.explanation: q0 is the control and q1 is the target. The target is flipped conditional on the control's computational-basis value.

questions.prompt: Starting from 00, which state does X(q0) prepare?
questions.explanation: The rightmost bit is q0 under the declared convention. Flipping it changes 00 to 01.

questions.prompt: What does CX(q0,q1) do to input 11?
questions.explanation: The control q0 is 1, so q1 flips from 1 to 0. The control itself remains 1.

questions.prompt: If q1 is |0> and q0 is |+>, what is the ordered joint vector?
questions.explanation: Only 00 and 01 occur because q1 remains zero. The tensor factors follow q1 then q0.

questions.prompt: What are the logical gate count and minimum depth of H(q0), H(q1), then CX(q0,q1), allowing disjoint gates in parallel?
questions.explanation: The two H gates occupy one layer because their targets are disjoint. CX uses both qubits and occupies a second layer.

questions.prompt: For q1 vector [sqrt(3)/2,1/2] and q0 vector [1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2)], what is P(10)?
questions.explanation: The amplitude of 10 is (1/2)(1/sqrt(2)). Its squared magnitude is 1/8; using q1=0 would instead give 3/8.

questions.prompt: Does applying CX(q0,q1) to 01 create entanglement?

options.text: No; the output 11 remains a product state
Yes; every two-qubit gate creates entanglement
Yes; any flipped target is entangled
No; CX can never create entanglement

questions.explanation: This input produces a single basis state, |1> tensor |1>. Entangling ability depends on the input, not only the gate name.

questions.prompt: Why is 01 a better bit-order test than the Bell outcomes 00 and 11?

options.text: Reversing 01 changes it to 10, while 00 and 11 are unchanged
Reversing a Bell histogram always changes its probabilities

questions.explanation: An asymmetric input exposes a reversed convention. Agreement on symmetric outputs alone can hide an ordering bug.
